title: Critical Appraisal in Ten Minutes — Is This Trial Worth Believing?

hook.en: Every week someone says, "A new study proves this treatment works." Sometimes it does. Often it does not. You do not need a statistics degree to tell the difference. You need ten minutes and six questions.
hook.ur: Har haftay koi kehta hai, "Nayi study ne sabit kar diya ke yeh ilaaj kaam karta hai." Kabhi karta hai. Aksar nahi. Farq pehchanne ke liye statistics ki degree nahi chahiye. Das minute aur chhe sawal chahiye.

goal.en: By the end, you'll appraise a treatment trial with six questions (RACE-C), read a confidence interval against a clinically important change, spot spin in an abstract, and decide whether a trial should change your practice.
goal.ur: End tak aap chhe sawalon (RACE-C) se ilaaj ke trial ko parkhenge, confidence interval ko clinically ahem tabdeeli ke mukable mein parhenge, abstract mein spin pehchanenge, aur tay karenge ke trial aap ki practice badle ya nahi.

text.en: **Critical appraisal** means checking a study before you trust it. Every appraisal asks three things: **Is it believable (valid)? What did it find? Does it apply to my patient?** A study can be honest and still not apply to your patient, and a study can be about your patient and still be too biased to believe. Ten minutes is enough to spot the major problems.
text.ur: **Critical appraisal** ka matlab hai study par bharosa karne se pehle usay jaanchna. Har appraisal teen sawal poochhti hai: **Kya yeh qabil-e-yaqeen (valid) hai? Isne kya paya? Kya yeh mere mareez par lagu hoti hai?** Study imaandar ho kar bhi aap ke mareez par lagu na ho sakti hai, aur study aap ke mareez ke baare mein ho kar bhi itni biased ho sakti hai ke yaqeen na ho. Bari kharabiyan pakadne ke liye das minute kaafi hain.

text.en: Think of **buying a used car**. You check the engine, the history and whether it fits your needs before you pay. A trial is the same: do not buy the conclusion just because the advertisement (the abstract) looks shiny. Look under the bonnet first.
text.ur: **Istemal shuda gaari khareedne** ko sochein. Paisa dene se pehle engine, tareekh aur apni zaroorat ke mutabiq hone ko dekhte hain. Trial bhi aisa hi hai: sirf is liye nateeja na kharidein ke ishtihaar (abstract) chamakta hai. Pehle bonnet ke neeche dekhein.

steps.title: Minute 1 to 2: the question and the claim
steps.detail: Who were the patients, what was compared with what, what was measured, and for how long? If you cannot say this in one sentence, the paper is unclear. || Minute 1 se 2: sawal aur dawa

steps.title: Minute 3 to 6: the methods (the RACE-C questions)
steps.detail: Randomised? Allocation hidden? Comparable groups? Eyes masked (assessors)? Completed follow-up? Confidence interval reported? || Minute 3 se 6: methods (RACE-C sawal)

steps.title: Minute 7 to 8: the result
steps.detail: Find the difference between groups and its confidence interval. Compare it with the smallest change that matters to patients. || Minute 7 se 8: nateeja

steps.title: Minute 9 to 10: will it help my patient?
steps.detail: Are my patients like theirs, is the treatment possible for me, and are the benefits worth the cost and risks? || Minute 9 se 10: kya mere mareez ko faida hoga?

title.en: The six RACE-C questions: what to look for, and what a problem looks like
title.ur: Chhe RACE-C sawal: kya dekhein, aur masla kaisa lagta hai

rows.en: Participants were assigned by chance, with a described method
rows.ur: Mareez ittifaq se tay kiye gaye, tareeqa bayan kiya gaya

rows.en: Allocation by the therapist, by day of the week or by choice
rows.ur: Therapist ne, hafte ke din ya pasand se tay kiya

rows.en: Sealed envelopes or a central system, so no one knew the next group
rows.ur: Sealed envelopes ya central system, koi agla group nahi jaanta tha

rows.en: Not mentioned, or the person enrolling could see the list
rows.ur: Zikr nahi, ya enroll karne wale ko list nazar aati thi

rows.en: Similar age, severity and baseline scores in each group
rows.ur: Har group mein umar, shiddat aur shuruaati scores milte julte

rows.en: Large differences at the start that favour one group
rows.ur: Shuru mein bade farq jo ek group ko faida dete hain

rows.en: The person who measured the outcome did not know the group
rows.ur: Jis ne nateeja naapa usay group maloom nahi tha

rows.en: The treating therapist also measured results, or patients rated their own pain with no masking
rows.ur: Ilaaj karne wale ne hi nateeja naapa, ya mareezon ne bina masking apna dard khud rate kiya

rows.en: Almost everyone was measured at the end, and the analysis kept them in their original groups
rows.ur: Taqreeban sab ko aakhir mein naapa gaya, aur analysis ne unhein apne asal groups mein rakha

rows.en: Many dropped out, especially from one group, or people were removed from the analysis
rows.ur: Bohat se chhor gaye, khaaskar ek group se, ya logon ko analysis se hata diya gaya

rows.en: A range that shows how precise the result is and whether it includes a worthwhile effect
rows.ur: Ek range jo nateeje ki durusti aur ahem asar ki maujoodgi dikhati hai

rows.en: Only a p-value, or "significant" with no range
rows.ur: Sirf p-value, ya "significant" bina range ke

question.en: A trial of a new exercise programme found a 6-point improvement in pain (on a 0 to 100 scale) with a confidence interval of 1 to 11. The smallest change patients said was worthwhile was 15 points. What is the best summary?
question.ur: Nayi exercise programme ke trial mein dard (0 se 100 scale par) mein 6 point behtari mili jiska confidence interval 1 se 11 tha. Mareezon ne jo sab se chhoti qabil-e-qadr tabdeeli batayi woh 15 point thi. Behtareen khulasa kya hai?

text.en: The programme clearly works and should be adopted everywhere
text.ur: Programme saaf kaam karta hai aur har jagah apnana chahiye

feedback.en: The improvement does not reach the size that matters.
feedback.ur: Behtari us size tak nahi pohanchti jo ahem hai.

text.en: The effect may be statistically detectable but is too small to matter to most patients
text.ur: Asar shumariyati taur par maloom ho sakta hai lekin zyada tar mareezon ke liye ahem hone se bohat chhota hai

feedback.en: Yes — even the top of the interval (11) falls short of the change that patients said mattered (15).
feedback.ur: Haan — interval ka oopar wala hissa (11) bhi us tabdeeli se kam hai jo mareezon ne ahem batayi (15).

text.en: The study proves the programme is harmful
text.ur: Study sabit karti hai ke programme nuqsan deh hai

feedback.en: Nothing in the result suggests harm.
feedback.ur: Nateeje mein nuqsan ka koi ishara nahi.

question.en: In a trial of a manual therapy technique, the therapist who delivered the technique also measured the patient's range of motion at the end. Which RACE-C question is this a problem for?
question.ur: Manual therapy ke trial mein jis therapist ne technique di usi ne aakhir mein range of motion naapi. Yeh RACE-C ke kaun se sawal ke liye masla hai?

text.en: R: Randomised, because the therapist was involved
text.ur: R: Randomised, kyunke therapist shamil tha

feedback.en: Randomisation is about how patients were assigned, not about who measured.
feedback.ur: Randomisation ka taalluq mareez tay karne se hai, naapne wale se nahi.

text.en: E: Eyes masked, because the assessor knew which group the patient was in and could influence the result
text.ur: E: Aankhein mehfooz, kyunke assessor ko group maloom tha aur nateeje par asar daal sakta tha

feedback.en: Yes — an unmasked assessor can unconsciously measure in favour of the treatment.
feedback.ur: Haan — be-naqab assessor ghair irada taur par ilaaj ke haq mein naap sakta hai.

text.en: C: Confidence interval, because range is always wide
text.ur: C: Confidence interval, kyunke range hamesha wasi hoti hai

feedback.en: The confidence interval is a separate question.

question.en: A trial lost 40 percent of one group and 8 percent of the other, and then analysed only those who finished. What is the biggest concern?
question.ur: Ek trial mein ek group ke 40 fisadi aur doosre ke 8 fisadi mareez chhor gaye, aur phir sirf mukammal karne walon ka analysis hua. Sab se bari fikr kya hai?

text.en: Larger numbers always make a trial more reliable
text.ur: Bade numbers hamesha trial ko zyada bharosemand banate hain

feedback.en: Size does not fix unequal drop-out.
feedback.ur: Size ghair barabar chhorne ko theek nahi karta.

text.en: There is no concern if the finishers improved
text.ur: Koi fikr nahi agar mukammal karne walon ne behtari ki

feedback.en: Improvement among finishers is exactly what attrition can exaggerate.
feedback.ur: Mukammal karne walon ki behtari wohi cheez hai jo attrition barha kar dikha sakta hai.

text.en: Attrition bias: the people who left may have differed, so the result can be wrong
text.ur: Attrition bias: jo log chhor gaye woh mukhtalif ho sakte hain, isliye nateeja ghalat ho sakta hai

feedback.en: Yes — uneven drop-out and analysing only completers can distort the result.
feedback.ur: Haan — ghair barabar chhorna aur sirf mukammal karne walon ka analysis nateeje ko bigad sakta hai.

text.en: **Reading only the abstract and the conclusion.** The abstract is the advertisement, and spin can turn a null result into "a promising trend". Look for words such as "tended to", "showed a trend", "numerically better" when the difference was not significant, a conclusion that goes beyond the data, and a headline about a secondary outcome. Always read the methods and the result before the conclusion.
text.ur: **Sirf abstract aur conclusion parhna.** Abstract ishtihaar hai, aur spin ghair-asar wale nateeje ko "ummeed afza rujhan" bana sakti hai. Aise alfaaz dekhein jaise "tended to", "showed a trend", "numerically better" jab farq significant nahi tha, aisa conclusion jo data se aage nikal jaye, aur secondary outcome par sar-khat. Conclusion se pehle hamesha methods aur nateeja parhein.

text.en: **Say what the evidence says, in plain words.** For example: "The best studies suggest this treatment helps a little for some people. It is not a miracle, and a few people feel no difference. Here is what we can try, how we will know whether it is working, and when we will change." This builds trust, because it tells the truth with warmth.
text.ur: **Evidence jo kehta hai saade alfaaz mein kahein.** Misaal: "Behtareen studies ishara karti hain ke yeh ilaaj kuch logon ko thora faida deta hai. Yeh mojiza nahi, aur kuch logon ko farq mehsoos nahi hota. Yeh hai jo hum aazma sakte hain, kaise pata chalega ke kaam kar raha hai, aur kab hum tabdeel karenge." Isse bharosa banta hai, kyunke yeh sach narmi se batata hai.

question.en: Why do small, single trials often show bigger effects than later large trials?
question.ur: Chhote, akele trials aksar baad ke bade trials se zyada bara asar kyun dikhate hain?

answer.en: Small trials are noisier, so chance alone produces some big effects, and the big ones are the ones that get published and noticed. Later larger trials usually find smaller effects. This is why one small positive trial should interest you but not yet change your practice; look for replication, a systematic review or a guideline.
answer.ur: Chhote trials zyada shor wale hote hain, isliye ittifaq akela kuch bare asar paida kar deta hai, aur bare asar wale hi shaya aur nazar mein aate hain. Baad ke bade trials aam taur par chhote asar paate hain. Isi liye ek chhota musbat trial aap ko dilchaspi de, lekin abhi aap ki practice na badle; dohrane, systematic review ya guideline dhoondein.

beats.patient: A press release says, "Ultrasound therapy cuts shoulder pain." The trial had 40 patients, was not masked, 12 of 20 in the control group dropped out, and the abstract reports a "trend towards improvement" with p = 0.09.
beats.assessment: Several RACE-C problems: no masking of assessors, large unequal drop-out and a result that did not reach significance, with spin in the wording.
beats.treatment: Do not change practice because of it. Note the question, look for a larger well-run trial or a systematic review, and keep using treatments with stronger evidence while you look.
beats.reassess: You find a larger masked trial and a review: the effect is small and unclear. You explain this honestly to patients who ask about ultrasound.

text.en: **Evidence is not a replacement for care.** Do not drop a safe, helpful treatment because a single trial was negative, and do not adopt a risky one because a single trial was positive. When a result affects safety, such as a manipulation or a medicine, check more than one source and talk to a senior clinician.
text.ur: **Evidence dekh-bhal ki jagah nahi leta.** Ek trial ke negative aane par mehfooz, mufeed ilaaj na chhorein, aur ek trial ke musbat aane par khatarnak ilaaj na apnayein. Jab nateeja hifazat ko chhoota ho, jaise manipulation ya dawai, to ek se zyada zarai dekhein aur kisi senior clinician se baat karein.

text.en: The Cochrane risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2) assesses randomised trials across five areas: the randomisation process, deviations from the intended intervention, missing outcome data, measurement of the outcome and selection of the reported result. The CONSORT statement lists what a trial report should contain, so that readers can judge it. As a rule of thumb, attrition under about five percent rarely matters and above about twenty percent is a serious threat; these are conventions, not laws.
text.ur: Cochrane ka risk-of-bias tool (RoB 2) randomised trials ko paanch hissoon mein parkhta hai: randomisation ka amal, irada kiye gaye ilaaj se inhiraf, ghayab outcome data, outcome ki pemaish aur shaya shuda nateeje ka intikhab. CONSORT statement batata hai ke trial ki report mein kya hona chahiye taake parhne wala jaanch sake. Andaze ke taur par takreeban paanch fisad se kam attrition shayad hi maayne rakhta hai aur takreeban bees fisad se zyada bara khatra hai; yeh riwayat hain, qanoon nahi.

text.en: **RACE-C.** Randomised, Allocation hidden, Comparable groups, Eyes masked, Completed follow-up, Confidence interval. Then ask the last question: will it help my patient?
text.ur: **RACE-C.** Randomised, Allocation chhupa hua, Comparable groups, Eyes masked, Completed follow-up, Confidence interval. Phir aakhri sawal poochhein: kya mere mareez ko faida hoga?

summary.en: Appraise with three questions: is it valid, what did it find, does it apply to my patient.
summary.ur: Teen sawalon se parkhein: kya valid hai, isne kya paya, kya mere mareez par lagu hota hai.

summary.en: Use RACE-C to check the methods, and compare the confidence interval with the smallest change that matters to patients.
summary.ur: Methods jaanchne ke liye RACE-C istemal karein, aur confidence interval ko us sab se chhoti tabdeeli se milayein jo mareezon ke liye ahem hai.

summary.en: Read beyond the abstract, watch for spin, and never change practice on one small trial.
summary.ur: Abstract se aage parhein, spin se khabardar rahein, aur ek chhote trial par practice na badlein.

back.en: Randomised, Allocation hidden, Comparable groups, Eyes masked, Completed follow-up, Confidence interval.
back.ur: Randomised, Allocation chhupa hua, Comparable groups, Eyes masked, Completed follow-up, Confidence interval.

front.en: What do you compare a confidence interval with?
front.ur: Confidence interval ko kis se milate hain?

back.en: The smallest change that matters to patients.
back.ur: Us sab se chhoti tabdeeli se jo mareezon ke liye ahem ho.

front.en: Name a sign of spin in an abstract.
front.ur: Abstract mein spin ki ek nishani batayein.

back.en: Calling a non-significant result a "trend" or promising.
back.ur: Ghair-significant nateeje ko "rujhan" ya ummeed afza kehna.

front.en: Why can unequal drop-out bias a trial?
front.ur: Ghair barabar chhorna trial ko biased kyun karta hai?

back.en: The people who leave may differ from those who stay.
back.ur: Jo log chhorte hain woh rukne walon se mukhtalif ho sakte hain.

note.en: A fuller walk through a trial report.
note.ur: Trial report ka mazeed tafseeli jaiza.
